claim_ceiling: The audit proves exact official-source observations and binding implementation decisions at the recorded retrieval time.

The v22 receipt proves that pinned Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Arena, the DROID Franka-Robotiq asset, PhysX, and Isaac Sim RTX reached build, exact reset, zero-action step, strict can stability, and two-camera tensor retention together at the sealed-SAGE-validated 0.50 meter base standoff.

The v19 and v21 receipts show that both the all-zero and measured-open Robotiq resets left the prior 0.40 meter base standoff in near contact; v22 validates only the 0.50 meter reset and physics-step condition, not task solvability.

The evidence rejects OVRTX for this exact Aura Gaussian-surflet asset after the preregistered v10 run returned black RGB and no positive finite metric depth; it does not reject OVRTX for its documented supported representations.

The official native Aura renderer reproduced both frozen exact-camera RGB references byte-for-byte and returned positive finite metric expected depth for every pixel; this establishes only standalone construction equivalence at those two cameras, not live Aura and Isaac composition, useful wrist-camera framing, scripted task success, ovphysx execution, or either learned policy.
It does not establish policy validity, generalization, physical transfer, fresh partner evidence, or production readiness.
Arena remains an alpha internal compositional dependency under Blueprint's existing evaluation and receipt contracts.

decisions: Use ManagerBasedRLEnvCfg and manager terms as the default harness architecture.
Separate scene, embodiment, task, observations, actions, events, terminations, and evaluation concerns.
Prove configuration, reset, step, and one-action reachability before policy work.
Once structured paid-runtime phases exist, require a new structured phase to extend the no-progress watchdog; arbitrary SSH, telemetry, or stdout noise is not progress.
Persist every redacted provider-log snapshot so interruption or TTL teardown retains the last completed scientific phase.
Use Arena's public Object SPAWNER composition seam for the required light instead of importing the unrelated full asset registry.
Encode approach, grasp, lift, translate, place, and settle as explicit task phases.
Compute success and terminal failures from deterministic simulator state rather than visual or policy judgment.
Use explicit EventManager prestartup, startup, reset, and interval modes.
Resolve every scored factor and seed before execution and reject invalid combinations fail-closed.
Bind Franka and Robotiq actuator limits and camera contracts in the embodiment layer.
Validate observation shape, device, timing, calibration, camera memory, and exact lossless retention before policy admission.
Convert simulator-native Warp arrays explicitly at the policy and receipt adapter boundary before indexing or Torch operations.

Follow the exact official Gaussian camera test asset at current develop revision 01eb210728ae6a1bd3cba854f31d21c614cbe4b0 by binding ParticleFieldEmissive.mdl with inverse tonemap and sRGB linearization disabled; retain Aura's sealed raw model and reject the converted layer until exact-camera visual conformance passes.
Select PhysX for the ADP-009D task and centralize its settings in one validated configuration.
Treat backend selection as a manifest-bound decision, not scattered runtime conditionals.
Keep the sealed can bytes immutable while applying the required PhysxSDFMeshCollisionAPI and explicit SDF cooking settings through a deterministic digest-bound composition layer.
Validate both the composed and live spawned collider, subscribe to native Kit logs, and fail closed on any automatic collision-approximation fallback before an episode is admissible.
Treat a static SDF-schema pass followed by collision-cooking timeout as infrastructure evidence only; it does not prove live collider, reset, or contact behavior.

After v14 passed static SAGE and the complete Arena import preflight, it remained inside environment construction for more than seventeen minutes with UJITSO stuck-build messages and a dead cooking child; preserve that as invalid infrastructure evidence, not a SAGE, can, reset, or policy result.

Apply NVIDIA's documented stuck-simulation diagnostic by disabling SETTING_UJITSO_COLLISION_COOKING before scene construction and using the legacy cooker, while keeping every collider byte, approximation token, and cooking parameter unchanged.

Require the resolved UJITSO setting and cooker identity in the native receipt; live collider validation and no-fallback checks remain mandatory, so changing the cooker cannot admit an episode by itself.

The v15 native microcheck resolved UJITSO false, built the same manager-based environment in 41.396117 seconds, validated the exact-v2 SDF can and 15 static SAGE triangle meshes live, completed two resets, one zero-action step, and two-camera retention, then tore down at 0.309049 USD with provider-zero observed.

Treat v15 as infrastructure reachability only: its receipt exposed that Arena release/0.2.1 did not reach the requested canonical joint pose and the wrist frame omitted the can, so bind the articulation initial state explicitly and fail closed on reset or hold-pose error before policy admission.

The v16 exact-joint-map probe correctly failed before reset because updating Arena's regex defaults created overlapping matches; replace the entire joint-position map instead of updating it. The run cost 0.221264 USD and provider-zero was observed.

The v17 replacement-map probe reached both native construction and the reset gate, then rejected the stock live arm pose at 1.152022362 radians maximum error. The run cost 0.067609 USD and provider-zero was observed.

Inspection of the exact pinned Isaac Lab reset implementation showed that Arena's first event updates only the default-joint buffer and its second event writes that buffer into simulation. Retain the second EventManager reset event with zero mean and zero standard deviation rather than disabling it.

The v18 EventManager-writer probe reached the requested pose exactly on both resets, held it within 0.000179053 radians, completed the native camera path, and preserved the v2 SDF can and task-envelope SAGE topology without warnings. It also measured a 0.197880811 meter XY can displacement and about 89.9986 degrees of tilt during nominal hold, so the prior reset pose is contact-invalid and may not be frozen as the canonical anchor.

The v19 official Arena arm-pose probe reduced can XY motion to 0.000011980 meters but tilted the can 6.188034 degrees because Arena's all-joint reset wrote zero into every Robotiq closed-loop joint. Retain the exact official seven-joint arm pose and use the contact-stable open-gripper coordinates measured in v15 as the smallest documented Arena compatibility exception; re-probe before admission.

The v21 measured-open-gripper reprobe still tilted the can 6.254314 degrees with only 0.000121966 meters XY motion, proving the 0.40 meter base standoff remains a near-contact start after reset/action application. Do not relax the gate. Shift the preregistered fixed base 0.10 meters away only after the sealed SAGE analysis confirms 5/5 footprint support, zero triangle overlap, and a 0.50 meter target distance inside the admitted Franka reach envelope; re-probe natively.

The v22 contact-clear-base reprobe validated that smallest change: with the same official Arena arm pose, measured-open Robotiq state, exact-v2 SDF can, and task-envelope SAGE topology, the can moved 0.000000533 meters XY and 0.000003636 meters vertically and tilted 0.009498 degrees. Admit the 0.50 meter base standoff for reset and physics stepping while retaining wrist-camera and live Aura composition blockers.
Label the historical convex-hull native probe as approximation-only and prohibit it from substituting for exact-v2 SDF admission.

Use the pinned Isaac Lab selective installer for assets, physx, tasks, and teleop only; retain the installer-required isaaclab_newton compatibility package without selecting Newton runtime extras or the Newton backend.
Install Isaac Lab Arena runtime dependencies without its development extra and reject any worker plan that silently expands to all Isaac Lab extensions or RL frameworks.
Do not add PresetCfg aliases until two genuine supported backend or configuration variants exist.
The initial ADP-009D runtime has one exact PhysX configuration.

OVRTX guidance was followed for the bounded preregistered exact-camera diagnostic, but OVRTX is rejected for the sealed Aura background after it returned black RGB and no positive finite metric depth for the exact Gaussian-surflet asset.

The failed diagnostic loaded the digest-bound Gaussian-surflet USDC through an attached ovstage ordinal and preserved the sealed Aura PLY unchanged; future OVRTX use remains representation-specific and cannot override this observed blocker.
Create OVRTX before any possible future OvPhysX initialization; the first bounded renderer microcheck intentionally loads no OvPhysX.
Attach one ovstage, load the immutable scene at ordinal one, advance the write floor, and destroy renderer and stage explicitly.
Author render settings on each RenderProduct, never as unsupported renderer-global configuration.
Bind path-tracing samples per pixel for PT, reset after camera or setting changes, and use the RTPT warmup contract for the live path.
Apply OmniRtxSettingsParticleFieldAPI_1 to the RenderProduct and bind accumulated Gaussian depth, accumulated albedo, and the documented 48-Gaussian accumulation default explicitly.
Request only LdrColor and metric DistanceToCameraSD for the Aura background probe; dynamic semantics remain owned by the Isaac layer.
Reject unitless DepthSD in configuration, execution receipts, and hybrid composition.
Map each requested CPU output, copy the DLPack array before retention, then unmap and destroy renderer-owned resources.
Record device, synchronization, map/unmap balance, array shape, dtype, and lossless output identities.
Advance the attached stage write floor before stepping and pass the same resolved ordinal to every warmup and capture step.
A loaded stage or single unvalidated frame cannot clear the renderer gate; both external and wrist RGB plus metric depth must pass.
Use the skill-documented 40-frame default for each RTPT camera after load and reset.
Use one PT step with an explicit RenderProduct samples-per-pixel value rather than treating repeated steps as PT sample control.
The Aura background owns no dynamic semantic IDs; robot and task-object labels remain in a composed Isaac override layer.
Never write semantic labels into the sealed Aura, SAGE, can, or cousin source assets.
Use CAD-to-SimReady only for a newly admitted cousin with explicit source, rights, runtime, and evidence.
Never mutate or replace the sealed approved can through a Content Agent.
Take a measured baseline before applying any USD performance mutation.
The first exact-v2 SDF run passed static schema validation but exceeded the intended 30-minute no-progress boundary during collision cooking before live-collider or reset proof.
After that baseline, remove only the unrelated Arena asset-registry import through its public SPAWNER seam; do not mutate the sealed can or exact registered SAGE collision bytes.
The measured SAGE baseline contains 165 static collision meshes, 509268 points, and 993678 faces; 164 meshes author convexDecomposition despite no SAGE prim carrying PhysicsRigidBodyAPI.

Follow Isaac Lab's official static-collider guidance by composing a deterministic runtime override that uses the exact SAGE triangle meshes for every active static environment collider while leaving the sealed SAGE bytes unchanged.

Fail closed unless the composed layer preserves the exact topology counts and transforms, disables only the sealed source target, preserves the support collider, contains no SAGE rigid body, and resolves every active SAGE mesh to the triangle-mesh approximation token none.

The first static-triangle measurement removed convex-decomposition fallback but remained inside environment build after more than ten minutes and emitted PhysX's explicit TriangleMesh triangles-are-too-big stability warning; this is invalid infrastructure evidence, not a successful startup.
Reject PhysX triangle-size stability warnings in the reusable runtime even if reset or stepping later becomes reachable.

Use only an immutable, digest-bound cooked USD or local-mesh-cache derivative tied to the exact source digest, Isaac Sim image, PhysX version, and runtime settings to avoid repeated cooking; a cache hit must still pass exact live topology and no-warning validation.
Do not decimate, merge, deduplicate, crop, or otherwise change SAGE geometry for this fix; measure native build, reset, step, and camera timing before any further optimization.

The static-triangle measurement subsequently hit the frozen 30-minute no-log-progress watchdog during environment build, cost 0.495256 USD, reached neither reset nor camera proof, and tore down with provider-zero observed.
Apply the smallest measured exception after that baseline: retain the full sealed SAGE bytes, but materialize a deterministic collision derivative for the preregistered Franka swept envelope only.

Select source meshes by exact world-space AABB intersection with the frozen task ROI, always include the registered support, exclude the replaced source can, and deactivate all out-of-envelope collision meshes.

The first mesh-level task-envelope derivative retained 99228 faces because any intersecting source mesh was kept whole; it removed the explicit triangle-size warning but remained inside environment build until the five-minute no-log-progress watchdog, cost 0.253793 USD, reached neither reset nor camera proof, and tore down with provider-zero observed.

Correct the measured mesh-level envelope bug by clipping every source triangle against the exact frozen task AABB, triangulating only the coplanar source-surface polygon inside the box, and then applying longest-edge midpoint refinement with a 0.5 meter edge ceiling.
Fail closed on selected/clipped/derived face counts, source-prim mapping, clipped/derived surface-area error above 1e-6, edge-limit failure, digest mismatch, or any live PhysX collision warning.

The corrected derivative binds 47359 selected source faces, 24248 exact clipped source faces, 26828 derived faces, 80484 points, 26.28230143 square meters of in-envelope source surface, and 9.22785062228535e-8 relative surface-area error.

Use canonical USDA text for the collision derivative because two semantically identical USDC Crate files built at different paths had different byte digests; byte-deterministic artifact identity takes precedence over the smaller binary encoding.
Limit claims from this derivative to the preregistered Franka task envelope; it is not whole-scene navigation or general SAGE collision proof.

The corrected v14 run passed the complete pinned dependency probe, Kit startup, static SAGE topology, and Arena environment import closure, then stalled in manager-based environment construction under UJITSO for more than seventeen minutes; it was interrupted at 0.243828 USD and all allocator-created instances were destroyed.

Use the official legacy-cooker switch as the smallest measured performance diagnostic before considering any further geometry change; the sealed v2 can, its original 65516-face SDF collider, and the task-area SAGE derivative remain byte-identical.

The v15 legacy-cooker run completed manager-based construction in 41.396117 seconds without collision fallback or triangle-stability warnings; preserve its exact receipt as the measured basis for keeping this centralized PhysX setting.
Preserve scientific identity and digest bindings across any later optimization.
Do not build an interactive realtime viewer because it is not an explicit deliverable.
A viewer may never replace lossless external and wrist policy-input media.

runtime_compatibility_decision.co_resident_runtime_status: PhysX and Isaac Sim RTX native build, exact reset, zero-action step, strict can stability, and camera tensor retention passed together at the v22 contact-clear 0.50 meter base standoff. OVRTX loaded all 415265 sealed Aura surflets, but the fully preregistered exact-camera v10 execution returned black color and no positive finite metric depth for either camera, so OVRTX is rejected for this sealed Aura representation. The official native Aura source at f23b26c subsequently reproduced both frozen 2048x1536 native reference frames byte-for-byte and returned positive finite metric expected camera-space depth for every pixel; the code-derived conformance receipt passed the preregistered thresholds. SAGE remains registered geometry, collision, and depth-reference only and may not replace Aura as policy-visible appearance. This standalone renderer gate did not execute Isaac composition, the wrist camera still omits the can in the retained v22 frame, and live Aura plus Isaac depth composition remains required before policy admission.

depth_convention_defect.defect: Aura publishes camera-Z surface depth (surf_depth_expected_camera_z_m) while Isaac publishes ray-length distance_to_camera; the composer compared them directly.
depth_convention_defect.effect: Dynamic-layer depth was inflated by 1/cos(theta), up to 1.7767x at the corners of the admitted 1280x720 DROID intrinsics, fabricating occlusion.
depth_convention_defect.fix: Every layer declares its depth geometry and is normalised to camera_z using the admitted pinhole intrinsics before any depth ordering.
depth_convention_defect.physical_validation: A robot standing in front of the room must have zero pixels occluded by the room background; the corrected comparison yields exactly zero.

retained_aura_surface_localisation.interpretation: The post-inpainting Aura asset removed the source can's appearance but retains reconstructed surface geometry co-located with it: a shell about 3.4 cm from the can axis at the can's own height, against a 3.1 cm visible radius for the approved can. Only 18.3% of occluded pixels are legitimate shelf-contact occlusion at the base; the remainder is retained phantom geometry. This is consistent with the retained ADP-009B receipt recording successful_inpainting_admitted false.
